title.narrative: Guinea Bissau: The Quality Education for All Project

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to improve the teaching and learning environment in grades 1-4 in targeted schools in Guinea-Bissau.

The development objective of the Quality Education for All Project for Guinea Bissau is to improve the teaching and learning environment in grades 1 to 4 in targeted schools in Guinea-Bissau. The project comprises of three components. The first component, strengthen school-based management practices and empower communities aims to improve the teaching and learning environment in targeted schools by: encouraging greater community participation in school management; and by providing fiscal resources at the school-level to purchase basic supplies, pedagogical materials, and to cover operating costs. It consists of following sub-components: (i) establishment of school management committees (SMCs); (ii) school grants program; and (iii) school inspection and system monitoring and evaluation. The second component, improve the quality of instruction will: (i) establish standards and harmonize the system for teacher training in order to reduce the frequency of teacher strikes; (ii) update the school curriculum; (iii) improve in-service teachers content knowledge and skills to effectively teach basic literacy and numeracy; and (iv) improve student learning outcomes in Portuguese and Mathematics in early grades. It consists of following sub-components: (i) teacher certification; (ii) in-service teacher training; (iii) scripted teaching lessons and interactive audio instruction (IAI); and (iv) learning materials for the new curriculum in grades 1 to 4. The third component, learning materials for the new curriculum in grades 1 to 4 aim is to improve the overall functioning of the education system by increasing the availability of data to guide decision-making and by strengthening the overall capacity of the ministry of education. It consists of following sub-components: (i) sector studies; and (ii) project management.

condition.narrative: Beginning in the Fiscal Year during which the Financing becomes effective, the Recipient shall, not later than November 15 in eachFiscal Year, prepare and furnish to the Association, a proposed annual work program and budget (“Annual Work Program and Budget”)for the next following Fiscal Year, giving details of: (a) a time table of programs and activities scheduled for implementation inthe course of that next following Fiscal Year; and (b) the estimated cost of each such program or activity, along with the budgetline item and source of funding corresponding to each program or activity. (IDA: Schedule 2.IV.B.1; GPE: Schedule 2.IV.A.1)

The Recipient shall establish and thereafter maintain a Project Implementation Unit (PIU), whose mandate, terms of reference andcomposition shall be acceptable to the Association, to be responsible for the day-to-day implementation of the Project, including:(i) responsibility for the fiduciary obligations under the Project; (ii) provision of technical support for implementation ofProject activities; (iii) preparation and management of bidding processes; (iv) management of project resources and ensuring thatdisbursements are made in accordance with the agreed procedures and practices; (v) preparation of quarterly and annual financialstatements; and (vi) provision of support to MEESJCD in overall M&E, including the collection and analysis of relevant data fortracking progress. (IDA and GPE Schedule 2.I.A.1(b))

The Recipient shall establish and thereafter maintain a Project Steering Committee (PSC), whose mandate, terms of reference andcomposition shall be acceptable to the Association, to be chaired by a representative of MEESJCD, and consisting of representativesof agencies and directorates involved in the implementation of the Project, to be responsible for strategic guidance and oversightof the Project, and coordination with other ongoing programs, including: (i) review and approval of AWPBs; (ii) review of progressreports, including quarterly budget execution reports; and (iii) monitoring and assessment of implementation progress and results.(IDA and GPE: Schedule 2.I.A.1(a))

The Recipient shall, not later than six (6) months after the Effective Date, recruit, on terms and conditions acceptable to theAssociation, an external auditor having qualifications and experience acceptable to the Association. (IDA: Schedule 2.IV.A; GPE:Schedule 2.II.B.4)

title.narrative: Number of primary schools with grades 1-4 using the new curriculum and IAI

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. All 560 schools targeted by the project started to implement the new curriculum in 2023/24. Due to procurement delays for the printing of the teachers guides and textbooks, teachers were using electronic copies of the guides and students only received handouts for 2023/24. However, the printed copies of the teacher guides and student manuals were delivered as expected at the beginning of the 2024/25 school year.

Target exceeded. The project reached 110,581 beneficiaries significantly surpassing the original target of 77,090. The number of students in Grades 1-4 was higher than expected when the Project was prepared/approved due to the actual number of students in the targeted schools. The original number of teachers was significantly surpassed due to newly hired teachers and the subsequent expansion of the Interactive Audio Instruction (IAI) Program and training in Information and Communication Technology (ICT) and in Gender-Based Violence (GBV) which was delivered to teachers in all 11 regions. Additional direct project beneficiaries included: (i) central MEN staff; (ii) Regional Directorate of Education staff within the five targeted regions; (iii) MEN staff which received training in HR Management, improved inspection practices, and the new textbook policies; and (iv) education staff, school directors, teachers, and community members who received training in the new SMC policy and manual.

title.narrative: Number of school inspectors' visits to targeted schools

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. For the inspectorate, tablets were purchased, electronic questionnaires developed, and motorcycles delivered to inspectors in the 5 regions targeted by the project. The inspection tool was developed via Kobo Toolbox and inspectors trained in its use. Inspection visits began to take place in all 5 regions in March 2023 - by June 2024 the target for number of visits was surpassed and all schools targeted by the project have been visited multiple times to validate school level data and monitor use of the new curriculum. The inspection surveys are administered via Kobo Toolbox which has helped to keep track of visits conducted and improve accountability.

Target exceeded. The original teacher training program started in 2021 and ended in early 2024. It included 3,015 teachers teaching Grades 1-4 from all 560 schools in the 5 regions targeted by the Project. Subsequently, due to some significant cost-savings from the textbook procurement, it was possible to: (i) deliver the planned week long training in ICT/IAI program and in GBV prevention not only to the teachers in the 5 targeted regions but to all teachers in Grades 1-4; and (ii) launch the scale up of the teacher training program on the new curriculum to the 6 regions not initially targeted by the Project. Hence, the teachers reached a total of 5,808 surpassing the target.

title.narrative: Percentage of grade 2 students in targeted schools with improved content knowledge in Portuguese and Mathematics

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. A pre-test to measure student learning in the 10 schools participating in the pilot of the new curriculum was administered among all students in Grades 1-4 at the end of the 2022/23 school year. The same Grade 2 tests in Mathematics and Portuguese were applied to Grade 3 students in the 10 pilot schools in late June 2024 to determine the percentage of students showing improvements. Of the 509 students tested, 66.6% demonstrated improvements in Portuguese and 71.4% demonstrated improvements in Mathematics. The average for the two subjects is 69% surpassing the target of 60%. The disaggregated results show slightly higher improvements among girls.

title.narrative: Percentage of grade 2 students in targeted schools with improved content knowledge in Portuguese and Mathematics

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. A pre-test to measure student learning in the 10 schools participating in the pilot of the new curriculum was administered among all students in grades 1-4 at the end of the 2022/23 school year. The same grade 2 tests in Mathematics and Portuguese were applied to Grade 3 students in the 10 pilot schools in late June 2024 to determine the percentage of students showing improvements. Of the 509 students tested, 66.6% demonstrated improvements in Portuguese and 71.4% demonstrated improvements in Mathematics. The average for the two subjects is 69% surpassing the target of 60%. The disaggregated results show slightly higher improvements for girls and geographic differences. A more thorough analysis of the results will be included as part of the ICR. There may also be the opportunity to analyze the results on learning outcomes from the PASEC pilot administered in May 2024 for the ICR.

title.narrative: Percentage of teachers who received in-service training under the project with improved content knowledge in Portuguese and Mathematics

comment.narrative: Target exceeded. A pre-test for teachers was administered at the beginning of training sessions in September 2022 to a sample of teachers in all five regions targeted by the Project to establish the baseline for teachers content knowledge in Portuguese and Mathematics. The post-training test was administered April 2024 at the conclusion of the program. The final results show the percentage of teachers who improved in Portuguese to be 73.2% and 90% in Mathematics. A non-weighted average of scores from both subjects is 81.8%. The tests at the end of each 1-2 week session also demonstrated consistent improvements.

title.narrative: National teacher evaluation tools and processes/procedures established

comment.narrative: Not achieved. A strategic decision between the World Bank and Ministry of Education was made to prioritize the establishment of a new Directorate for HR, create a reliable HR database, and conduct census taking activities for teachers. These activities have directly led to more stability in the sector with teachers paid on time, successful application of the Teacher Career Law, and a dramatic reduction in teacher strikes. The days of teacher strikes went from 85 in 2018/19 (nearly 40% of the school year) to less than 9% in 2023/24. The activity to develop the procedures for teacher evaluations was transferred to the Public Sector Strengthening Project which provides significant support for the HR reforms in education. It is expected to be completed in full but not under the timeline for the Quality Education for All Project.

title.narrative: PASEC II learning assessment in grades 2 and 5 conducted and results disseminated

comment.narrative: Partially achieved (on track to be achieved in full). Guinea-Bissau's application to participate as formal members in PASEC 2024 was accepted in early 2023. The Project is financing the work from 2023 until October 2024 when the project closes. Another source of financing was identified to cover the other expenses until 2026. Unfortunately, the timing for the official PASEC did not align with the timeline for implementation of the project and data from the assessment won't be available until late 2025. However, opposed to implementing a stand-alone, adapted PASEC II, official membership/participation comes with the key advantages including being more sustainable and the results will be comparable across countries and can be used for benchmarking exercises like the World Bank's Human Capital Index.

title.narrative: National textbook policy and dissemination plan adopted

comment.narrative: Partially achieved (and expected to be achieved in full). The diagnostic on textbook distribution was finalized; the textbook dissemination plan was developed and used to guide the textbook dissemination for the 2024/25 school year; and a draft version of the new textbook policy was developed and revised. Adoption of the final version of the policy is expected no later than December 2024.

title.narrative: National textbook policy and dissemination plan adopted

comment.narrative: Target achieved. The diagnostic on textbook distribution was finalized; the textbook dissemination plan was developed and used to guide the textbook dissemination for the 2024/25 school year; and a draft version of the new textbook policy was developed and revised prior to the Project's closing date of October 31, 2025. The final version of National Textbook Policy and dissemination plan was adopted by the Government in late March 2025 and training on its use was provided in April 2025 by using funds from the, GPE-Financed, and World Bank managed, Institutional Strengthening and the Quality Education for All Project (PRIEQT, P176697).

title.narrative: Basic education statistics for 5 regions targeted by the project available annually

comment.narrative: Target achieved. Using an electronic rapid survey based on GEMS, a report with basic education statistics for the 5 regions targeted by the Project was completed in 2021, 2022, 2023, and 2024. The quality and reliability of the data has improved with each round. This data has improved the delivery of teacher training activities, the implementation of the new curriculum in Grades 1-4, and to expand use of the new curriculum and improve planning in the sector.
